title: Purification and processing of blood-forming tissue units, the haematons, in searching for mammalian stem cell niches
protocol: Euthanize mice by injecting i.p. 12.5 µg Avertin in 100 µl NaCl per 10 g body weight or use 1.5-2% isoflurane inhalation.
Shave the mouse with an electric trimmer.
Disinfect the shaved area in 70% (vol/vol) ethanol for 1 min.
Immobilize the mouse at the back-down position on a dissection pad using elastic rings by the fore and hind limbs.
Place the platform under a viewer light source.
Cut the skin from the pubis along the sternum to the wall of the abdomen using scissors and forceps.
Fix the skin aside with pins.
Pull the liver carefully.
Cut the diaphragm.
Cut the ribs along the chondro-osseous joints bilaterally.
Turn up and immobilize the sternum by a needle (G 22) to uncover the heart.
Rinse the thorax and abdomen with Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺-free PBS supplemented with 10 mM EDTA.
Lift the liver and digestive tube gently to facilitate trans-cardiac perfusion.
Keep main blood vessels intact.
Avoid visceral tissues from compressing.
Hold the heart with lightweight tweezers.
Introduce the butterfly cannula via the heart apex and left ventricle into the ascending aorta.
Hole the right atrium.
Perfuse mice with 20-30 ml pre-warmed 0.9% (wt/vol) NaCl (37°C, 110 cm height/pressure).
Strip the hind limbs.
Dissect femurs aseptically and cut muscle and tendon under 4 ml PBS containing 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA and double strength antibiotic-antimycotic solution at +4°C in a 60 mm Petri dish.
Detach and remove the distal epiphysis.
Rinse the cleaned femurs.
Transfer cleaned femurs to a 35 mm Petri dish containing 4 ml IMDM with 4% (vol/vol) FCS.
Place the dish under the dissection microscope.
Hold the femur firmly with serrated forceps.
Section the distal spongiosa in halves.
Bisect the compact diaphysis bone longitudinally.
Make tiny, continuous holes using a sharp scalpel along one side of the femur.
Make tiny, continuous holes along the opposite side of the femur.
Open the two halves to uncover the BM shaft.
Change medium to remove joint, bone spikes or muscle fragments prior to BM fractionation.
Bisect femurs in perinatal and young mice using watchmaker forceps and 25 G needle.
Aspirate bone marrow (BM) shaft from the central diaphysis using a 200-μl pipette tip and transfer it into Tube-B.
Dilacerate metaphyseal spongiosa by fine scalpels to open the spongy meshwork.
Remove loosely attached suspension and hematopoietic nodules by harmless trituration and pool this fraction in Tube-B.
Scrape out the whole inner endosteal/spongy bone cushion and transfer it into Tube-C.
Separate the whole, pooled BM parenchyma into two fractions.
Dissociate and erode the whole BM by three up-and-down aspirations via a 23 G needle.
Allow nodules to settle for 10 minutes on ice.
Transfer the supernatant suspensions in a 15-ml tube.
Add 1 ml fresh medium to the pellet.
Repeat the dispersion/erosion step two times using 25 G needles.
Pool the supernatant suspensions to constitute the buffy coat fraction.
Conserve the nodular pellet containing haematons.
Stir up the purified haematon pellet in 1 ml standard culture medium.
Transfer 50 μl aliquot on a cleaned glass slide.
Remove occasional bone spikes and bubbles under the stereomicroscope.
Cover the preparation with a 60x25 mm cover slip.
Count compact aggregates under the microscope at low magnification.
Continue mild dispersion through a 25G needle if necessary.
Plate aliquots in Hydron bordered 25-sq cm flask filled with 4 ml My-LTCM.
Incubate cultures in a CO2 incubator at 33 °C.
Count haematons appearing as rolling/slightly adherent spheroids or fully adherent cobblestone area forming islands under the phase-contrast inverted microscope.
Continue culture and apply weekly half depopulation and replacement of medium by fresh My-LTCM.
Count CAFIs again at d35.
Spin down the BC, haematon, and endosteum fractions for 7 minutes at 400g.
Discard the supernatants.
Add 200 µl of enzyme cocktail (0.1% wt/vol collagenase type-I, -II, -IV and 10 I.U. DNase-I) to one femur equivalent pellet.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Triturate cells using a 200-µl silicon-coated pipette tip every 5-10 minutes during incubation.
Stop the digestion by adding 2 ml of ice-cold IMDM containing 2% (vol/vol) FCS.
Let resistant aggregates settle down for 5 minutes.
Transfer supernatants to new 4-ml tubes labelled respectively as Pool-A, B, and C at +4°C.
Add 200 µl of collagenase-dispase-hyaluronidase solution to the residual aggregates.
Incubate for an additional 8 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer the suspension to POOL tubes.
Dilute with 4 ml IMDM containing 2% (vol/vol) FCS on ice.
Centrifuge at 400g for 7 minutes at +4°C.
Wash the pellets twice in IMDM containing 2% (vol/vol) FCS.
Filter through a 30-µm mesh nylon filter.
Count nucleated cells in a haemocytometer using RBC lysis solution and then adjust cell concentration to 0.5-1x10^6 cells per ml PBS containing 4% (vol/vol) FCS.
Transfer 10 ml suspensions in conical 15-ml tubes.
Add 5 μL Hoechst_33342 stock solution (10 mg/ml) per 10 ml cell suspension and incubate samples at 37 °C in the dark for 60 min; suspend cells at 15 min intervals.
Chill samples on ice, spin down cells for 7 min at 400g at +4 °C and then wash the pellet once in 12 ml PBS containing 4% (vol/vol) FCS.
Discard the supernatant and leave 50 μl staining medium over the cells.
Remix cells in 200 μl medium and add 5 μl biotin-conjugated lineage marker antibodies.
Incubate cells on ice for 30 min then wash twice with 10 ml medium.
Stir up 10^7 cells in 90 µl PBS containing 5% (vol/vol) normal rat serum and 0.05% (wt/vol) NaN3.
Add streptavidin-APC-Cy7, anti-Sca-1, anti-c-kit, and anti-CD150 antibody stock reagents on ice to the cells.
Incubate cells on ice for 60 min.
Add 10 µl of 7-AAD stock solution during the last 10 minutes of incubation.
Dilute samples with 4 ml of ice-cold IMDM containing 4% (vol/vol) FCS.
Filter suspensions through 40-µm nylon meshes in 4-ml polystyrene FACS tubes.
Spin down cells and discard the supernatant.
Suspend cells in 1 ml of IMDM complemented with 4% (vol/vol) FCS on ice for immediate analysis and sorting by FACSvantage.
Sort presumptive HSCs (Sp-KSL) ≥ 10^3 cells per fraction in ice-cold PBS supplemented with 4% (vol/vol) FCS.
Keep sorted cells at 4 °C for 15-45 min to minimize cell shape deformations.
Spin down the cells at 400g for 7 minutes.
Suspend the pellet in 5 ml of cold 4% (wt/vol) PFA for 10 minutes.
Spin down the fixed cells then suspend the pellet gently in 200 μl staining buffer (PBS) containing 10 μg/ml Hoechst33342 and 1.0 μg/ml Pyronin-Y.
Stain the cells for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the stained cells in 5 ml of PBS.
Analyse PY and Hoechst blue fluorescence by FACS.

Sort presumptive HSCs (e.g., Sp-KSL) individually into round-bottomed 96-well plates previously filled with 150 μl My-LTCM supplemented with early acting growth factors (40 ng mSCF, 10 ng mVEGF, 10 ng mFlt3-L, 5 ng hTPO and 5 ng hIL-11).
Incubate the cells at 37 °C in humidified air with 5% CO2.
Count cells in wells initially at 12-24 hour intervals under an inverted microscope.
Estimate cell numbers between about 300 and 30,000 cells per well using colony radius calculations (n=r^2π).
For colonies exceeding 30,000 cells per well (i.e., when r≥100), count from small (e.g., 15 μl) aliquots following suspension.
Split individual cultures in aliquots by transferring one-third of the suspensions to new wells containing 100 µl cytokine-supplemented fresh medium.
Continue cell production in each well until the acrophase and decline of the actuary growth curve.
Analyze clones according to length of cell-cycle quiescence, expansion potential, total cell number, and phenotype (Giemsa-stained spin preparation; FACS).
Irradiate wild-type male host mice (C57/B6-CD45.2 phenotype; 2-4 months old) at 9.5 Gy on day -1 of graft injection.
Sort increasing numbers of presumptive HSCs, i.e., 10, 30, or 90 Lin^-neg^SpSK cells, into individual wells containing 100 µl IMDM with 0.5% (vol/vol) BSA for CFUs and CRU assays.
Add 10^5 normal competitor C57/B6-CD45.2 BM cells in 100 µl IMDM containing 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA to the sorted donor cells per well.
Inject the total cell mixture in 200 µl i.v. using a 30G (0.3x8 mm) insulin syringe via the retro-orbital plexus.
Perform spleen colony-forming unit (CFU-S_d12_) assay, splenectomy, and identification of ROSA-26 donor-derived colonies.
Conduct CMRA assay.
Take 50 μl peripheral blood from the retro-orbital plexus into heparinised syringes.
Dilute blood in 1 ml PBS containing 20 IU heparin and keep on ice until processing.
Centrifuge at 400g for 5 min then carefully remove the supernatant.
Remix pellet for 5 sec then add 1.6 ml RBC lysis buffer for 2 min at RT.
Stop osmotic lyses immediately when red colour turns deeper by adding 200 μl FCS and centrifuge cells at 4°C.
Remix the pellet in ice-cold 1 ml PBS containing 4% \(vol/vol) FCS.
Analyse donor derived cells by FACS using rat anti-mouse CD45.1, FITC conjugated antibody or fluorescent substrate FDG (FITC channel).
Quantify B-cells by B220 (APC) and myeloid cells by CD11b (Gr) (PE) RaM antibodies.
Detect intracellular FDG positive cells according to the protocol provided by Molecular Probes/Invitrogen.
Apply standard statistical methods for calculation cell frequency or CMRA.
Apply coloured hydrogel angiography to reveal tissue units in solid organs and haematon units related to the vascular system along the femur.
Bisect the femur following hydrogel casting and Zn-7 fixation, wash in pH 6.2 buffer, and remove loosely attached cells by gentle agitation through a 200-μl pipette in a Petri dish.
Replace buffer with acetyl-cholinesterase reaction solution for 3-4 h at room temperature in the dark.
Wash the preparation in Tris buffer and fix again in Zn-7 at room temperature for 30 min, dehydrate in 30%, 50%, and 70% ethanol for 30 min each, then rehydrate in 100 mM Tris at pH8.1.
Aspirate washing buffer and add 5 ml alkaline phosphatase reaction solution until background colouration starts to appear (usually 30-40 min).
Stain bone with Alizarin red and cartilage with Alcian blue overnight at 37 °C.
Clear background colouration by repeated changes in 1% KOH/20% glycerin bath.
Clear the sample in 1% KOH, then analyse and photograph the tissue under dark-field stereomicroscopy.
Fix haematons in Zn-7 for 4-24 h at 4 °C.
Wash the fixed haematons three times for 1 hour each in 100 mM Tris-HCl buffer pH7.5.
Manipulate haematon isolates using silicon-coated pipette tips and centrifuge tubes.
Immerse haematon particles in a fine sheet of alginate hydrogel.
Saturate non-specific binding sites in 100 mM Tris-HCl buffer (pH7.5), 0.9% (wt/vol) NaCl containing 2% (vol/vol) normal rat serum (TNRS) for 2 hours.
Add biotinylated rat anti-Tie2 monoclonal antibody (1:50 dilution) to the alginate-embedded haematon preparation in TNRS buffer and incubate for 2 hours.
Wash three times, each for 20 minutes, in 2 ml of buffer at 4 °C.
Incubate with streptavidin-APC/Cy7 diluted 1:100 in TNRS buffer along with fluorochrome-labelled primary rat antibodies to Sca-1 (1:100 FITC), c-kit (1:100 PE), and CD150 (1:50 APC).
Incubate the preparation with DAPI at a concentration of 1.0 μg ml⁻¹ for 30 minutes.
Wash the sheet of haematons twice, each for 1 hour, in TNRS buffer.
Remove buffer completely using a 30G needle.
Add 50 µl Mowiol prior to transferring and mounting on microscope slides.
Label niche-forming cells and intracellular components.
Fix haematons with Zn-7 and wash them.
Dehydrate haematons through 30%, then 50% ethanol for 15 minutes each, followed by 70% ethanol for 60 minutes.
Store samples overnight in 70% ethanol at 4 °C if necessary.
Rehydrate fixed haematons in Tris-HCl buffer.
Incubate rehydrated haematons in TAT washing buffer containing normal blocking serum.
Pellet identical cohorts of haematon particles for parallel labeling.
Add primary antibody to the pellet in a dilution range from 1/20 to 1/100, with 1 μg Ab per 10^6 cells, and incubate for 6-16 hours.
Wash the pellet three times in TAT buffer containing normal serum for 30 minutes each time.
Add biotin-conjugated secondary antibody at a dilution of 1/100, and incubate for 4-6 hours before washing twice with TAT buffer.
Incubate samples in TAT buffer supplemented with normal rat serum for 60 minutes.

Mix in streptavidin conjugates (2 µl streptavidin-PE or streptavidin-Alexa-546) and fluorochrome-conjugated primary antibodies (Sca1-FITC, CD150-APC) in TAT buffer containing 5% normal rat serum for 6-16 hours.
Add DAPI at a concentration of 1.0 µg ml-1 to the samples and incubate for 30 minutes if desired.
Wash samples three times with TAT buffer for 1 hour each at 4 °C.
Proceed montage for LSCM analysis.
Transfer hematons in 40 μl Mowiol on a clean Superfrost slide.
Remove occasional thick clumps under the stereomicroscope.
Place the coverslip (15x15 mm) and stick it with nail polish to hinder evaporation.
Acquire image series under the LSCM.
Produce 3D animation using LSM510 software v3.0.
Adjust brightness and color balance for figure preparation using Adobe Photoshop vCS3.
Fix haematon isolates in 2% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde or 4% (wt/vol) glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M Na-cacodylate buffer (pH 7.2) for 2-4 h at +4°C.
Wash the haematon pellet three times for 1 hour each in Ca-free buffer at +4°C.
Admix 1% (wt/vol) alginate pre-polymer in 0.9% NaCl (wt/vol) to protect haematons from disintegration.
Collect haematons on a 30 μm mesh filter.
Polymerize the filter-retained haematons in a thin layer of alginate using a 0.9% NaCl bath containing 10 mM CaCl₂.
Identify representative haematons and cut them with the alginate layer under a stereomicroscope for processing.
Dehydrate samples in graded series of ethanol and propylene dioxide.
Proceed with inclusion according to standard technique provided by the manufacturer.
Cut semi-thin (0.5-1 μm) or ultrathin (gold to silver colour) sections with a Reichert-UM2 microtome.
Collect semi-thin sections on a clean microscope slide and collect thin sections on formvar-coated micro-grids, respectively.
Stain semi-thin sections in hematoxilin/fast green or 2% toluidine blue solution containing 60% sucrose at 90°C for 2 min.
Stain thin sections with uranyl acetate followed by lead citrate.
Study samples under a JEOL 100C EM at 100-kV accelerating voltage.
Dissect the bone sample and remove surrounding soft tissues.
Dehydrate the bone in 30%, 50%, and 70% (vol/vol) ethanol for one hour each.
Rehydrate the bone in distilled water to minimize deformation during measurement.
Insert firmly a tiny, short pin at one side of the bone.
Seal the end on the central holder using light-curing bonding resin (Heliobond, Vivadent).
Scan immobilized bone samples at 360° rotation at 0.7 degree intervals.
Reconstruct 2D and 3D images using the cone beam volumetric algorithm (Feldkamp).
Measure total bone volume on the computer-reconstructed 3D samples.
Measure total "empty" volume corresponding to the BM parenchyma.
Measure surface of intersection, which corresponds to the endosteal and spongy bone surface.
Calculate trabecular separation using a plate model.
Calculate trabecular diameter using a rod model.
Calculate seven parameters for selected skeleton segments.
